name: Hollow Wells
summary: The greatest oasis of the Burning Sands and the southern terminus of the salt roads. Built around a ring of deep wells sunk into the floor of a buried Concord cistern, Hollow Wells is half living city, half excavation — its people dwell literally on top of the old world and sell pieces of it north.
role: caravan hub; well-capital of the sands

ruler.title: First Well-Sister
ruler.current: Well-Sister Mahal of the Deep Ring
ruler.note: Elected for life by the well-councils; can be un-elected by the same, which has happened twice in living memory.

districts.name: The Deep Ring
districts.description: The innermost circle of wells, tended by the Well-Sisters of Akhmat. Water is drawn at dawn and dusk only; drawing at night is theft of the goddess's tears.

districts.name: The Buried Gate
districts.description: The half-excavated mouth of a Concord city beneath the oasis. Licensed diggers work the upper strata; the lower galleries are sealed by common consent after the third disappearance.

districts.name: The Salt Market
districts.description: Where caravans water, rest, and trade: salt, glass, relics, and rumors. Prices are signed, not spoken — Hollow Sign was born here.

districts.name: The Tentspire
districts.description: The caravan quarter: a hill of tents and rope bridges that changes shape weekly. Permanent residents are outnumbered forty to one.

landmarks.name: Akhmat's Tears
landmarks.description: The deepest well, said to be wept by the goddess herself. Its water never diminishes — but last month, for the first time in living memory, it tasted of salt.

landmarks.name: The Relic Walk
landmarks.description: A colonnade of excavated Concord stonework lining the road north, each stone carved with the name of the digger who found it. The Censer wants it confiscated; the Well-Sisters refuse.

landmarks.name: The Listening Dune
landmarks.description: A dune outside the walls that never moves. Hollowborn say the buried city beneath it is listening; negotiators meet there when words must not be overheard by the living.

conflicts: Akhmat's Tears turned salty — the Well-Sisters do not believe the goddess did it, and are quietly investigating their own aquifer.
Censer agents press the Well-Sisters to surrender the Relic Walk and the Buried Gate's finds; the council refuses, citing the oath of the road.
Rememberers' cells operate in the lower galleries; the Well-Sisters know and permit it — the Edict of Silence has never sat well in the sands.
Water rights grow tense as northern demand rises with the Crownlands' growth.

inhabitants.note: Well-clans, diggers, and caravan houses; the city's bones are theirs.
Northern factors and a permanent Censer legation that is tolerated and never invited anywhere.
Deep-folk engineers who helped sink the modern wells; they consult on the Buried Gate's supports.
A single Verdant kin envoy maintains the desert-medicine trade. She plants one tree a year; eleven survive.
